named_other_account_applied.application: Its strict endpoint cap 2/3<p<7/9 sharpens the singleton-first-block ideal-cut empty-mass to 4/9<pi(empty)<7/9; its two active Hasse-blocker channels identify terminal-label information that a scalar cut-size statistic can lose.

new_result.name: width-two ideal-cut convolution
new_result.statement: If c is the first strong-majority element (hence minimal), Q=P\{c}, and S={z in Q:z||c}, then S is a width-at-most-two ideal and L(P) is in bijection with the disjoint union over ideals I of S of L(I) x {c} x L(Q\I). Thus e(P)=sum_I e(I)e(Q\I), with exact pair numerators obtained from uniform smaller-poset laws on I and Q\I plus deterministic cross-cut orientations.
new_result.hitting_time_form: For uniform tau in L(Q), if kappa is the initial S-prefix length before the first successor of c, then W_c(tau)=kappa+1 and Pr_P(A)-Pr_Q(A)=Cov_Q(1_A,kappa)/E_Q[kappa+1].
new_result.counterexample_constraint: In a hypothetical POS3 counterexample, pi(empty)>4/9, every cut inclusion marginal is <1/3, and E[kappa(kappa+1)] < (2|S|/3)E[kappa+1] < 3|S|/2.

refuted_shortcut.claim: all strong cross pairs force a balanced pair inside the width-two ideal S
refuted_shortcut.example: width-three 7-element poset with covers c<0,0<2,0<4,1<2,2<3; S={1,5}; Pr(c<1)=7/10, Pr(c<5)=57/70, but Pr(1<5)=24/35>2/3

first_missing_implication: Width-two ideal-cut selection lemma: among the uniform-balanced pairs of the smaller Q, choose one whose exact cut-mixture probability remains in [1/3,2/3], using the cut inclusion marginals, empty-cut atom, common majority orientation, and endpoint channel structure. Arbitrary fixed-pair transfer and localization to S are both false.
